declare(strict_types=1);

use AzGuard\Contracts\ContextGuard;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Tests\Stubs\ContextUser;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Tests\Stubs\Project;
use CoreX\Modules\Data\EntityDefinition;
use CoreX\Modules\Testing\ArrayEntityRegistry;

beforeEach(function (): void {
    app(ArrayEntityRegistry::class)->register(new EntityDefinition(
        handle: 'project',
        model: Project::class,
        table: 'projects',
        module: 'corex/access-tests',
        labelSingular: 'Project',
        labelPlural: 'Projects',
        capabilities: [],
        fields: [],
        titleAttribute: 'name',
    ));
    $this->guard = app(ContextGuard::class);
});

it('returns false when the context entity does not exist', function (): void {
    $user = new ContextUser(scoped: true, global: true);

    expect($this->guard->checkInContext($user, 'project', 'missing', 'crm.deal.view', 'app'))->toBeFalse();
});

it('returns false for an unknown context type', function (): void {
    $user = new ContextUser(scoped: true, global: true);

    expect($this->guard->checkInContext($user, 'unknown', '1', 'crm.deal.view', 'app'))->toBeFalse();
});

it('grants when the user has the permission scoped to the entity', function (): void {
    $project = Project::create(['name' => 'p']);
    $user = new ContextUser(scoped: true);

    expect($this->guard->checkInContext($user, 'project', $project->id, 'crm.deal.view', 'app'))->toBeTrue();
});

it('falls back to a global permission within the panel', function (): void {
    $project = Project::create(['name' => 'p']);
    $user = new ContextUser(global: true);

    expect($this->guard->checkInContext($user, 'project', $project->id, 'crm.deal.view', 'app'))->toBeTrue();
});

it('denies when the user has neither scoped nor global permission', function (): void {
    $project = Project::create(['name' => 'p']);
    $user = new ContextUser;

    expect($this->guard->checkInContext($user, 'project', $project->id, 'crm.deal.view', 'app'))->toBeFalse();
});

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Access\Extend\Internal;

use CoreX\Access\Contracts\RoleMatrixCompiler;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\EntityRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\ModuleRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\Events\ModuleDisabled;
use CoreX\Modules\Events\ModuleEnabled;

/**
 * Ties `aut_role_matrix` compilation to module lifecycle (AC-27, D112/D113):
 * on ANY enable/disable, {@see RoleMatrixCompiler::recompileAll()} re-runs,
 * so active-entity checks are re-evaluated against
 * the module's new state. This class creates NO `aut_role_matrix` rows
 * itself (D113 — the merger only merges the SURFACE, modules write the
 * matrix); the rows a disabled module's entities leave behind stay in the
 * table for re-enable.
 *
 * `merge()` also validates `CompiledRegistry::$permissions` declarations
 * against {@see EntityRegistry}: a declaration whose `entity` is unknown to
 * the registry cannot be attributed to any module (the compiled slot
 * carries no module attribution of its own, findings/P2.9-seam-inventory
 * §6) and is skipped fail-closed — surfaced as a warning in the return
 * value, never a log (same contract as {@see CoreX\Access\Matrix\Internal\MatrixValidator}).
 *
 * @internal spec: B-11 §4 п.2/п.4, P2.21 D112/D113, AC-27
 */
final readonly class PermissionsMerger
{
    public function __construct(
        private ModuleRegistry $modules,
        private EntityRegistry $entities,
        private RoleMatrixCompiler $compiler,
    ) {}

    public function __invoke(ModuleEnabled|ModuleDisabled $event): void
    {
        $this->merge();
    }

    /** @return list<string> warnings for Extend\Permissions declarations whose entity is unknown to EntityRegistry */
    public function merge(): array
    {
        $warnings = [];

        foreach ($this->modules->compiled()->permissions as $declaration) {
            if (! $this->entities->has($declaration->entity)) {
                $warnings[] = sprintf(
                    "Extend\\Permissions declares unknown entity '%s' — declaration ignored, no matrix row can attribute to a module.",
                    $declaration->entity,
                );
            }
        }

        $this->compiler->recompileAll();

        return $warnings;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace AzGuard\Models;

use AzGuard\Configuration\Config;
use AzGuard\Contracts\RoleInterface;
use AzGuard\Support\RoleIdentity;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\HasMany;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\MorphToMany;
use Illuminate\Support\Carbon;
use Override;

/**
 * @property int $id
 * @property string $name
 * @property int $level
 * @property string|null $class_name
 * @property Carbon|null $created_at
 * @property Carbon|null $updated_at
 */
class Role extends Model
{
    /**
     * class_name is deliberately NOT fillable (C-11): it wires the role to a
     * PHP RoleInterface class (getRoleLogic()) and must only be set through
     * trusted internal paths (e.g. RoleAssignmentCommand's direct setter),
     * never from mass-assigned request input.
     */
    protected $fillable = ['name', 'level'];

    #[Override]
    public function getTable(): string
    {
        return Config::rolesTable();
    }

    /** @return MorphToMany<Model, $this> */
    public function users(): MorphToMany
    {
        /** @var class-string<Model> $userModel */
        $userModel = config('auth.providers.users.model');

        return $this->morphedByMany(
            $userModel,
            'model',
            Config::modelHasRolesTable(),
            'role_id',
            'model_id',
        );
    }

    /**
     * Permissions assigned to the role via the DB (not via PHP class).
     * Used by DatabaseRoleGrantSource.
     *
     * @return HasMany<RolePermission, $this>
     */
    public function dbPermissions(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(
            Config::rolePermissionModel(),
            'role_id',
        );
    }

    /**
     * Instantiate the role logic class (e.g. SuperAdminRole).
     *
     * Returns null only for DB-only roles (`class_name` null). A non-null
     * missing or non-contract class raises InvalidRoleClassException.
     */
    public function getRoleLogic(): ?RoleInterface
    {
        if ($this->class_name === null) {
            return null;
        }

        return RoleIdentity::logicOrFail($this->class_name);
    }

    /**
     * Check whether the role has a DB permission for the given panel.
     */
    public function hasDbPermission(string $permissionKey, string $panelId): bool
    {
        return $this->dbPermissions()
            ->where('permission_key', $permissionKey)
            ->where('panel_id', $panelId)
            ->exists();
    }

    /**
     * Find a role by its name. Consolidates resolveRole() / resolveScopeRole() across traits.
     */
    public static function findByName(string $name): ?static
    {
        return static::query()->where('name', $name)->first();
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace AzGuard\Models;

use AzGuard\Configuration\Config;
use AzGuard\Contracts\RolePermissionValidator;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;
use Illuminate\Support\Carbon;
use Override;

/**
 * DB-level permissions assigned to a role via the role_permissions table.
 *
 * @property int $id
 * @property int $role_id
 * @property string $permission_key
 * @property string $panel_id
 * @property Carbon $created_at
 * @property Carbon $updated_at
 */
class RolePermission extends Model
{
    #[Override]
    public function getTable(): string
    {
        return Config::rolePermissionsTable();
    }

    protected $fillable = [
        'role_id',
        'permission_key',
        'panel_id',
    ];

    /**
     * Opt-in guard against un-linted permission keys. Off by default (lenient),
     * so existing behaviour is unchanged; when enabled, the swappable
     * {@see RolePermissionValidator} vets the key on every save.
     */
    #[Override]
    protected static function booted(): void
    {
        static::saving(static function (self $rolePermission): void {
            if (! Config::validateRolePermissionsEnabled()) {
                return;
            }

            app(RolePermissionValidator::class)->validate(
                (string) $rolePermission->permission_key,
                (string) $rolePermission->panel_id,
            );
        });
    }

    /** @return BelongsTo<Role, $this> */
    public function role(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Config::roleModel(), 'role_id');
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use AzGuard\Contracts\ContextGuard;
use AzGuard\Contracts\PermissionLayer;
use AzGuard\Models\Role;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\AccessAzguardRegistrar;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\AccessAzguardServiceProvider;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal\AccessAzguardOptions;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal\AzGuardRoleModel;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal\TenantContextGuard;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal\WorkspacePermissionLayer;
use CoreX\Config\Exceptions\InvalidConfiguration;
use Illuminate\Config\Repository;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Application;

it('resolves bridge options as a shared immutable snapshot', function (): void {
    $options = app(AccessAzguardOptions::class);
    config()->set('corex-access-azguard.azguard_pins.table_names.roles', 'changed_roles');

    expect(app(AccessAzguardOptions::class))->toBe($options)
        ->and($options->rolesTable)->toBe('az_guard_roles');
    expect(function () use ($options): void {
        $options->rolesTable = 'mutable_roles';
    })->toThrow(Error::class);
});

it('keeps the shared bridge options unresolved during registration', function (): void {
    $application = new Application;
    $application->instance('config', new Repository);
    (new AccessAzguardServiceProvider($application))->register();

    expect($application->resolved(AccessAzguardOptions::class))->toBeFalse();
    $application->make('config')->set('corex-access-azguard.bind_permission_layer', false);
    $options = $application->make(AccessAzguardOptions::class);
    expect($options->bindPermissionLayer)->toBeFalse()
        ->and($application->make(AccessAzguardOptions::class))->toBe($options);
});

it('applies bridge pins through the public registrar over conflicting AzGuard config', function (): void {
    config()->set('az-guard.table_names.roles', 'external_roles');
    config()->set('az-guard.column_names.morph_type', 'int');
    config()->set('az-guard.models.role', Role::class);
    config()->set('corex-access-azguard.azguard_pins.table_names.roles', 'bridge_roles');

    (new AccessAzguardRegistrar)->register($this->app);

    expect(config('az-guard.table_names.roles'))->toBe('bridge_roles')
        ->and(config('az-guard.column_names.morph_type'))->toBe('uuid')
        ->and(config('az-guard.models.role'))->toBe(AzGuardRoleModel::class)
        ->and(app(ContextGuard::class))->toBeInstanceOf(TenantContextGuard::class)
        ->and(app(PermissionLayer::class))->toBeInstanceOf(WorkspacePermissionLayer::class);
});

it('retains an existing permission layer binding when bridge binding is disabled', function (): void {
    config()->set('corex-access-azguard.bind_permission_layer', false);
    $layer = Mockery::mock(PermissionLayer::class);
    app()->instance(PermissionLayer::class, $layer);

    (new AccessAzguardRegistrar)->register($this->app);

    expect(app(PermissionLayer::class))->toBe($layer);
});

it('has usable bridge options defaults on an empty configuration', function (): void {
    $options = AccessAzguardOptions::fromArray([]);

    expect($options->bindPermissionLayer)->toBeTrue()
        ->and($options->rolesTable)->toBe('az_guard_roles')
        ->and($options->morphType)->toBe('uuid')
        ->and($options->roleModel)->toBe(AzGuardRoleModel::class);
});

it('accepts the documented AzGuard pin override shapes', function (): void {
    $options = AccessAzguardOptions::fromArray([
        'bind_permission_layer' => false,
        'azguard_pins' => [
            'table_names' => ['roles' => 'custom_roles'],
            'column_names' => ['morph_type' => 'ulid'],
            'models' => ['role' => Role::class],
        ],
    ]);

    expect($options->bindPermissionLayer)->toBeFalse()
        ->and($options->rolesTable)->toBe('custom_roles')
        ->and($options->morphType)->toBe('ulid')
        ->and($options->roleModel)->toBe(Role::class)
        ->and(AccessAzguardOptions::fromArray(['azguard_pins' => ['models' => ['role' => null]]])->roleModel)->toBeNull();
});

it('rejects invalid bridge configuration with the offending path', function (array $config, string $path): void {
    try {
        AccessAzguardOptions::fromArray($config);
        $this->fail('Invalid bridge configuration was accepted.');
    } catch (InvalidConfiguration $exception) {
        expect($exception->violations)->toHaveCount(1)
            ->and($exception->violations[0])->toStartWith($path.':');
    }
})->with([
    'binding flag' => [['bind_permission_layer' => 'true'], 'bind_permission_layer'],
    'pin group' => [['azguard_pins' => 'invalid'], 'azguard_pins'],
    'tables group' => [['azguard_pins' => ['table_names' => false]], 'azguard_pins.table_names'],
    'roles table' => [['azguard_pins' => ['table_names' => ['roles' => '']]], 'azguard_pins.table_names.roles'],
    'morph type' => [['azguard_pins' => ['column_names' => ['morph_type' => 'bad']]], 'azguard_pins.column_names.morph_type'],
    'role model' => [['azguard_pins' => ['models' => ['role' => stdClass::class]]], 'azguard_pins.models.role'],
]);

it('validates the lazy bridge options before booting runtime integrations', function (): void {
    $application = new Application;
    $application->instance('config', new Repository);
    $provider = new AccessAzguardServiceProvider($application);
    $provider->register();
    $application->make('config')->set('corex-access-azguard.bind_permission_layer', 'invalid');

    expect(fn () => $provider->boot())->toThrow(InvalidConfiguration::class);
});

availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. availableCommands.description: Learns how the user writes from their own sent messages and docs, and builds a voice profile so future drafts sound like them instead of generic AI. The profile is saved as the my-writing-style skill. Use when the user asks to set up, learn, or capture their writing voice, or complains that drafts sound generic or unlike them and no my-writing-style profile exists. Only for drafting text the user will send as themselves, not for Claude's own replies.

A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: user:docs
availableCommands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.

Loops until all reviewers find 0 issues of any severity.

availableCommands.name: learn

availableCommands.name: long-running-background-tasks

Use when: about to launch, supervise, inspect, diagnose, or report on work that keeps running after it is started.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Access\Laravel;

use CoreX\Access\Access\Internal\WorkspaceScopeWiring;
use CoreX\Access\Extend\Internal\PermissionsMerger;
use CoreX\Access\Identity\Laravel\PrincipalUserProvider;
use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\EntityRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\PackageRegistrar;
use CoreX\Modules\Events\ModuleDisabled;
use CoreX\Modules\Events\ModuleEnabled;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Foundation\Application;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Scope;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Event;
use InvalidArgumentException;
use Override;

#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Call, since: '1.0')]
final class AccessIntegrationRegistrar implements PackageRegistrar
{
    #[Override]
    public function register(Application $app): void {}

    #[Override]
    public function boot(Application $app): void
    {
        $this->registerIdentityProvider($app);

        WorkspaceScopeWiring::wire(
            $app->make(EntityRegistry::class),
            $app->make(AuthOptions::class)->workspaceScopeClass,
            static fn (string $class): Scope => self::workspaceScope($app, $class),
        );

        Event::listen(ModuleEnabled::class, PermissionsMerger::class);
        Event::listen(ModuleDisabled::class, PermissionsMerger::class);
    }

    /** @return Scope<Model> */
    private static function workspaceScope(Application $app, string $class): Scope
    {
        $scope = $app->make($class);

        if (! $scope instanceof Scope) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException("Workspace scope class [{$class}] must implement ".Scope::class.'.');
        }

        return $scope;
    }

    /**
     * Registers the `corex-principal` Laravel auth driver (D125) — never
     * touches `config('auth.*')` itself (a package does not impose the
     * consuming app's guard wiring); a consumer opts in with
     * `auth.providers.users.driver = 'corex-principal'` (see README).
     */
    private function registerIdentityProvider(Application $app): void
    {
        if (! $app->make(AuthOptions::class)->identityEnabled) {
            return;
        }

        Auth::provider('corex-principal', static fn (): PrincipalUserProvider => new PrincipalUserProvider(
            options: $app->make(AuthOptions::class),
        ));
    }
}

1→# Changelog

## Unreleased — native authorization (P07.4)

- Breaking before 1.0: access evaluates its own role matrix and direct grants; AzGuard integration moved to the optional `corex-access-azguard` package.
- Added `aut_direct_grants` and the `RoleMatrixCompiled` event. Compilation dispatches synchronously in the tenant transaction and invalidates scope versions after commit.
- Removed `aut_roles.azguard_role_id`, `RoleView::azguardRoleId`, `RoleMatrixData::bindAzGuardRole`, and AzGuard options. Access checks deny inactive entities before reading cached scopes or grants.

## Unreleased — thin providers and registrars (P05.2)
10→
- `CoreAuthServiceProvider` delegates to `AccessBindingsRegistrar` and `AccessIntegrationRegistrar`; bindings, order and lifetimes are unchanged.

## Unreleased — typed Options and runtime configuration checks (P05.1)

- `AuthOptions` is a lazy shared singleton resolved in `boot()`; it is no longer bound with `instance()` while the provider registers.

## Unreleased — kernel package and API migration

- Breaking (PLAN3.P02–P04, pre-1.0): Authorization now exposes Principal, RecordContext and AccessChecker ports plus typed AuthOptions and matrix registration; AzGuard identities and permission storage remain implementation details.
20→- Package installation uses the `axiomasoft` Composer vendor and PHP 8.4–8.5 / Laravel 12–13 constraints; `resources/contracts/php-api.json` records the explicitly attributed API and SPI. Old names have no compatibility aliases.

## Unreleased — PHP surface strict cutover

- Breaking (PLAN3.P04, pre-1.0): supported PHP symbols are declared individually with Api/Spi attributes. Concrete implementation types moved to Internal and typed ports/DTOs and error contracts replace predecessor surfaces as recorded in PLAN3.D63/D64; namespace metadata no longer grants compatibility.
- Generated `resources/contracts/php-api.json` records supported layers and signatures. Strict source/graph/BC checks enforce the declared surface; Internal has no external BC promise.

## Unreleased — typed error contract (P04.3)

- Added package owned error enums, definitions and safe coded exception descriptors.
30→- Error constructors require enum identities; existing error wire values are scoped.
- Contributions are validated and frozen at boot; persisted identities use validated lookup.

## Unreleased — package identifier alignment

### Changed

- PLAN3.D57: implementation classes moved to `<Module>\Internal\…`, public types to module categories
  (`Contracts|Data|Enums|Events|Exceptions`); see `docs/architecture/constitution.md` STR-003. Drain queues before
  upgrading; stored `*_type` values holding an old model FQCN no longer resolve (no aliases, PLAN3.D01).
40→
- Breaking before 1.0: Rename config and publish identifiers to `corex-access` and environment variables to `COREX_ACCESS_*`.

Все заметные изменения `corex/auth` документируются здесь. Формат — [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).
Пакет pre-1.0 — breaking-изменения публичных контрактов легальны в MINOR до 1.0 (D17).

## [Unreleased]

- PHP API manifests now record direct inheritance, interfaces and traits separately and include only members declared by this package; external dependency members are omitted without changing the `php-api/1` schema.

50→### Changed

- Password rehash delegates to the identity table owner's `IdentityPasswordRehasher` port with compare-and-swap inputs; auth no longer updates `users` directly.
- P7.7: `DefaultAccessChecker`, matrix/access helpers и компилятор матрицы
  получают `AuthOptions` вместо прямых вызовов `config('corex-auth.*')`.
- P7.6: `AuthOptions::fromArray` валидирует снимок `corex-auth`; провайдер и
  `PrincipalUserProvider` читают identity и pins из Options.
- Released metadata no longer declares development `path` repositories or an
  unconfirmed AzGuard remote. Private AzGuard resolution is a consumer-owned,
  canonical immutable channel; credentials are never stored in this package.
60→
## [0.1.0] - 2026-07-27

First tagged release — roadmap-фаза P1 / B-11 (AzGuard-мост, entity-scoped RBAC, OIDC).
Repo-level tag `v0.2.0` per D17 default policy (no per-package split mirror configured).

### Added

- **Local login lane / principal seam (P2.22, D125).** `Identity\PrincipalUserProvider
  implements Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\UserProvider` — all six interface methods, table/columns
70→  entirely from `config('corex-auth.identity')` (`connection`/`table`/column map), queries via
  `DB::connection($conn)->table($table)` (no `corex/tenancy` model import, AC-28). The "live
  user" filter (`active = true AND deleted_at IS NULL`) is applied in BOTH `retrieveById()` and
  `retrieveByCredentials()` — a deactivated user's live session does not outlive the
  deactivation. `retrieveByCredentials()` ignores the `password` key when building the WHERE
  (Laravel canon) and matches e-mail case-insensitively (`whereRaw('lower(...) = ?')` — the
  schema's unique index is exactly that). `validateCredentials()` is `Hash::check()` only, never
  a string comparison. `rehashPasswordIfRequired()` issues an `UPDATE` iff
  `Hash::needsRehash($hash) || $force`, otherwise zero queries. `retrieveByToken()`/
  `updateRememberToken()` are permanent no-ops — `users` (P2.7, frozen DDL) carries no
80→  `remember_token` column and one will not be added.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Access\Contracts;

use CoreX\Access\Data\RecordContext;
use CoreX\Access\Enums\Scope;
use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;

/**
 * Two-phase permission check (B-11 §5.5): allowed() is the capability gate
 * (native matrix and direct grants), scopeFor()/canOnRecord() apply the compiled
 * row-visibility scope on top. Implemented by P2.20's DefaultAccessChecker
 * over the schema/compiler produced by P2.8.
 */
#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Implement, since: '1.0')]
interface AccessChecker
{
    /** Capability check: can the principal do $action on the active entity type at all. */
    public function allowed(Principal $p, string $entityKey, string $action): bool;

    /** Effective scope: max weight of the principal's base matrix rows; a $ctx row overrides (may narrow) it. */
    public function scopeFor(Principal $p, string $entityKey, string $action, ?RecordContext $ctx = null): Scope;

    /** Record-level check: allowed() plus the effective scope's predicate against $record, or an active direct grant. */
    public function canOnRecord(Principal $p, string $action, object $record): bool;
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Access\Contracts;

use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;

/**
 * Publishes a native role matrix for one role inside a tenant transaction.
 * The scope-map version changes after the transaction commits.
 */
#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Implement, since: '1.0')]
interface RoleMatrixCompiler
{
    public function compile(string $roleId): void;

    /** Re-runs compile() for every non-deleted role — after a module install/enable (B-11 §4 п.2). */
    public function recompileAll(): void;
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace AzGuard\Contracts;

use AzGuard\Registry\Values\PermissionSet;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable;

/**
 * Optional post-aggregation hook applied by EffectivePermissionResolver after
 * it has unioned every GrantSource into the global PermissionSet.
 *
 * Unlike a GrantSource (which can only add permissions), a layer receives the
 * fully-resolved global set and may return a different set — so it can also
 * restrict, e.g. the context package narrowing the result to the active
 * workspace. Bind a single implementation to this interface to install it; with
 * none bound the resolver leaves the global set untouched.
 *
 * @api
 */
interface PermissionLayer
{
    public function apply(PermissionSet $global, Authenticatable $user, string $panelId): PermissionSet;

    /**
     * A string distinguishing cache entries when the layer's output depends on
     * out-of-band state (e.g. the active workspace context). Returned by the
     * resolver into the permission cache key so that, for example, workspace 42
     * and workspace 99 never share a cached set. Return '' when the layer adds
     * no cache-relevant state for this panel.
     */
    public function cacheDiscriminator(string $panelId): string;
}

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: bundled:review
availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). A bare /review defaults to reviewing your uncommitted working state when the tree is dirty, or your whole branch vs main when the tree is clean. Main, local, and branch modes write a review file plus a summary to disk. PR and stack modes post the findings as a PENDING GitHub review for the user to inspect and submit through the UI. Use --main for an explicit clean-tree branch review, --stack for stacked PRs, --submit to publish immediately as COMMENT, or --approve to publish and approve; the default remains PENDING.
